ocr_l1_t1.piece: Ustad Tari Khan, tabla solo in teentaal (16-beat cycle) with harmonium lehra, filmed at Darbar Festival. The performer speaks and recites the bols before playing.
questions: the first tabla stroke of the played performance, after any speech or vocal recitation of the bols
the moment the harmonium starts its repeating melodic cycle (lehra/nagma) underneath the tabla
the moment the tabla leaves the opening theme and begins faster, denser variations
the clearest point at which the playing becomes fastest and densest
the last tabla stroke of the performance
the moment the audience applause begins

ocr_l1_t2.piece: Balwinder Safri, 'Aaja Billo' - a 1990s UK bhangra track with dhol, tumbi, synthesisers, drum machine and Punjabi vocals.
questions: the end of the spoken English sample at the very start, where the music proper begins
the moment the full dance groove (dhol plus drum machine) locks in
the first statement of the repeated chorus hook
the clearest instrumental passage with no singing, where tumbi or dhol are exposed
the moment the music stops or has faded out completely

ocr_l2_t1.piece: Classical Arabic Orchestra of Aleppo: Samai Bayati. A free-rhythm oud taqsim, then the samai thaqil in a 10-beat cycle for the full takht ensemble (oud, qanun, ney, violin, riq, darabuka), then a faster closing section in 6/8 (samai darij).
questions: the first note of the solo oud improvisation
the moment the full ensemble and the percussion enter together and a regular rhythmic cycle begins
the clearest change of character in the middle of the ensemble music, where a contrasting section begins
the moment the music changes to the faster, lilting closing metre
the last note of the piece

ocr_l2_t2.piece: Orchestra Mesogios: Kalamatianos - an instrumental Greek folk dance in 7/8 (3+2+2) for clarinet, violin, santouri, laouto and tambourine.
questions: the first note of the music
the moment the clarinet takes the melodic lead
the moment the violin takes over the melodic lead from the clarinet
the moment a clearly different melodic strain or section begins
the last note of the piece

ocr_l3_t1.piece: Famoudou Konate with Ensemble Hamana Dan Ba: 'Matadi'. A Malinke drum ensemble from Guinea - djembe lead drum, dundun/sangban/kenkeni bass drums with attached bells, and call-and-response singing.
questions: the first sound: the lead djembe's opening call phrase
the moment the bells and bass drums have all entered and the full repeating groove is running
the first time the group chorus answers the lead singer
the clearest passage where the lead djembe solos over the ensemble with no singing
the last drum stroke of the piece

ocr_l3_t2.piece: Sona Jobarteh: 'Jarabi', a traditional Mande song, filmed by BBC News Africa. Kora (21-string harp) with guitar and calabash percussion, and Sona Jobarteh singing.
questions: the first note of the solo kora introduction
the moment the guitar and percussion join the kora
the clearest instrumental kora passage between sung sections
the last note of the performance

ocr_l4_t1.piece: Monobloco live: 'Peguei Um Ita No Norte (Explode Coracao)'. A Rio de Janeiro samba bateria - surdo, repinique, caixa, tamborim, agogo, ganza - with cavaquinho and sung verses and chorus.
questions: the first musical sound after any speech, where the band begins to play
the moment the whole percussion band is playing the groove together
the first time the crowd or chorus sings the main refrain
the clearest rhythmic break where the whole band stops or plays a unison figure
the last note of the performance

ocr_l4_t2.piece: Trinidad All Stars Steel Orchestra: 'Curry Tabanca', a Panorama calypso arrangement for steel orchestra with engine room (irons, scratcher, drum kit). There is a stage announcement before the music.
questions: the first note played by the steel orchestra, after any announcement
the moment the whole band including the engine room percussion is playing together
the first clear statement of the main calypso tune
the clearest change of key in the arrangement
the start of the closing section that drives to the end
the final chord of the performance
